hooks.text: Billions of planets drift through total darkness without any star at all.
Trillions of invisible worlds wander the dark void between stars.
Orphan planets likely outnumber star-bound worlds by six to one.

title: The Trillions of Starless Planets Drifting in the Dark
description: Billions of rogue planets wander the Milky Way in total darkness, and recent research suggests they outnumber star-bound worlds by six to one.

beats.text: Billions of planets drift through total darkness without any star at all.
beats.visual: Artist's concept of a rogue planet in deep space, NASA, 2020
queries: starless planet in deep space concept

beats.text: Most people assume every single planet belongs to a solar system bound tightly to a shining sun.
beats.visual: Artist's concept of a solar system with planets orbiting a star, NASA, 2018

beats.text: Instead, massive nomadic objects known as rogue planets wander the vast galaxy in absolute solitude.
Astronomers first identified a massive population of these mysterious objects back in 2011 using gravitational microlensing techniques.
beats.visual: Gravitational microlensing space-time warp diagram, ESO, 2011

beats.text: That clever observational technique reveals invisible worlds when their gravity warps the light of distant background stars.
beats.visual: Microlensing event illustration showing background star light bending, NASA, 2015

beats.text: Recent research suggests these lonely wanderers significantly outnumber star-bound worlds by six to one.
beats.visual: Terrestrial rogue planet illustration in dark space, NASA, 2022

beats.text: Trillions of invisible worlds continue drifting through total darkness without any star at all.
beats.visual: Starless rogue planet in deep space concept, ESO, 2019
